newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares down as dollar comes off highs.
newsitem.headline: German shares down as dollar comes off highs.

text.p: German shares retreated early on Wednesday as investors moved to take profits after the bourse reached an all-time high the day before.
The blue-chip DAX index slipped 18.05 points, or 0.63 percent, to 2,868.93 by 1040 GMT, after closing on Tuesday at a record high of 2,886.98.
The decline cames after Wall Street on Tuesday suffered its largest single-day setback since July. The Dow Jones index tumbled 79.01 points to close at 6,442.69.
An opening dip in the dollar below 1.56 marks also dampened export-dependent stocks like car maker BMW AG and chemical group BASF AG and drug maker Hoechst AG.

Shares in BMW, fell in IBIS trade, coming off highs reached in a late rally on Tuesday, but opened bourse dealings up 4.50 marks at 1,052 marks. Meanwhile, Hoechst fell 60 pfennigs to 68.60 marks and BASF, a recent favorite of investors, fell 45 pfennigs to 59.55 marks.
The dollar edged lower after German economic growth in the third quarter exceeded most expectations. Year-on-year gross domestic product growth doubled to 2.4 percent in the third quarter.
"It's consolidation today, based on where the dollar is going and the news that German GDP was a little better than expected," one Frankfurt trader said.
The better-than-expected GDP data also pulled German bonds off record highs.
Drugs group Schering AG stood out as one of the few gainers, rising 4.40 marks to 133.30 marks by 1040 GMT.

Dealers said the gain in the stock, which has added over ten percent in the last week alone, was prompted by one large buy order from a bank and said the stock was also supported by technical factors.
